name: IEC analogue multiplier element
summary: Analogue element with a multiplication mark whose output is proportional to the product of two inputs.
description: An analogue multiplier element produces an output proportional to the product of its inputs, usually scaled by a fixed factor such as one tenth of a volt per volt squared. IEC-style diagrams draw it as a rectangle with a multiplication mark; TI's logic overview uses the Greek capital pi as the multiplier qualifier in the digital context.

Multipliers appear in power calculation from voltage and current signals, modulators and gain-control circuits. The scale factor and the quadrant capability must be stated, because a one-quadrant device cannot handle negative inputs.
The element does not show accuracy or bandwidth. Those govern whether a hardware multiplier or a digital calculation is appropriate.
readingNotes: State scale factor and quadrant capability.
Identify which inputs carry voltage and current in power calculations.
distinction: A summing element adds signals; the multiplier forms their product.

facts.label: Function
facts.value: Product of inputs times scale factor
